Done. Efficiency measured, committed (d8b45bb, e150063, journal), 23/23 tests green, pyaot clean.

## Real time-to-result (wall-clock to 90% accuracy, training only, CPU)

| task | seed | double-decoder | baseline | steps (D vs B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3-digit | 1 | 7.4 s | **5.4 s** | 400 vs 400 |
| 3-digit | 2 | 8.0 s | **4.5 s** | 300 vs 300 |
| 5-digit | 1 | 23.8 s | **16.5 s** | 500 vs 600 |
| 5-digit | 2 | **11.5 s** | 20.8 s | 400 vs 1100 |

## Inference latency (trained models, ms)

| | baseline | double greedy | vote-of-8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3-digit, batch 500 | 22.0 | 46.8 | 424.8 |
| 3-digit, single prompt | 1.6 | 2.3 | 20.8 |
| 5-digit, batch 500 | 76.5 | 115.7 | 741.0 |
| 5-digit, single prompt | 3.1 | **3.3** | 30.3 |

## Honest read

1. **Training wall-clock: double-decoder loses unless its step advantage is big.** It trains two models sequentially (~1.7× per step), so equal step counts (3-digit) mean strictly slower. It only wins when decomposition slashes steps hard — 5-digit seed 2: 2.75× fewer steps → 1.8× faster to 90%.
2. **The tax is removable.** Thinker and talker are fully independent (talker trains on ground-truth thoughts, never thinker output) — train them in parallel on two devices and wall-clock becomes max() not sum(), flipping 3-digit to parity and widening the 5-digit win. Not measurable this session (GPU still fully occupied).
3. **Single-prompt inference is near-parity** (3.3 vs 3.1 ms at 5 digits): diffusion thinker costs 6 fixed parallel passes regardless of length while AR cost grows linearly with output — the structural advantage compounds with longer answers.
4. **Vote-of-8 costs ~10×** for marginal accuracy at converged models — only worth it with adaptive K (vote only when candidates disagree), untested.
5. High seed variance on time-to-90 (journaled); more seeds before strong claims.

Note: `make lint` currently fails repo-wide on `tests/test_clock_quantization.py` — a foreign agent's unformatted file, outside my scope, left untouched and journaled. My files pass.
